chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad from Al-Hasan ibn Ali from Hammad ibn 'Uthman from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) said:
The one who marries the woman but does not make it in his self that he would be giving her dower to her, so he is an adulterer.

key_terms.مَهْر: Dower or dowry given to the wife

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on marriage if the man does not intend to pay the dower?
ai.summary: In Shia jurisprudence, this hadith from al-Kafi highlights that the internal intention (niyyah) to pay the dower is a constitutive element of a valid marriage contract, not merely a subsequent obligation. By equating the marriage of a man who deceitfully withholds this intent to zina, the Imam underscores the seriousness of financial honesty in marital relations, a ruling often cited by jurists to distinguish between a simple debt and a fundamental defect in the contract's validity.
